parsed.use_case: A search service stores terms from product names, usernames, or commands and answers both exact-match lookups and “what entries begin with this text?” queries as a user types. The same structure supports efficient prefix-based routing and autocomplete over changing dictionaries.
system_examples: Elasticsearch completion suggester — indexes terms for prefix-based search-as-you-type suggestions.
Shell command completion — checks command names and paths against entered prefixes, while exact lookup validates a full command name.
parsed.explanation: A trie shares common prefixes among stored strings, so insert, exact search, and prefix checks take O(L) time for a word or prefix of length L, rather than scanning all N stored strings. This makes lookup time depend on the input length instead of dictionary size, though the nodes consume memory proportional to the total stored characters; production autocomplete systems often add ranking and filtering beyond this core.
